business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tailoring of Licensed Theatrical Costume Robes and Synthetic Wigs

Agreement between Samoa and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Protection of Investments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Act 2018 (SAM 2018), as amended; International Companies Act 1987, ss. 101–108 (custody of UBO records by registered agent); Money Laundering (Prescribed Transactions and Reporting) Regulations 2019; Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2021 (UBO return to the Registrar of International Companies)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (certified copy)
UBO Declaration / Register of Beneficial Owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered Agent (Licensed International Company Service Provider)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders holding 25% or more, and all ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and Samoa's Domestic List of Designated Persons issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons linked to China, the United Kingdom, and Pacific Island states. Screening results must be documented in the UBO file and retained for a minimum of five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry (SICR) e-services portal operated by the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Section 14(2) of the International Companies Act 1987, a company name may be in English, Samoan, or any other language using Latin script. Where a name includes Chinese or other non-Latin characters, it must also be rendered in a Latin-character transliteration for registry indexing. The registered name must not contain symbols, punctuation marks, or characters that are not accepted by the registry's digital indexing system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be appealed within 14 days by filing a Notice of Appeal with the Registrar, accompanied by a copy of the rejection letter and a fee of USD 25 (WST 50). The Registrar must issue a determination within 7 business days. If the appeal is unsuccessful, the applicant may petition the Minister of Commerce and Industry within 30 days of the determination. Name reservation may be extended for one further period of 30 days upon payment of 50% of the original reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted. Section 112 of the International Companies Act 1987 requires every International Company to maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the address of its licensed international company service provider. A post-office box alone is insufficient. Virtual office services are not accepted for the registered office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 1-3% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk internet retail apparel company with no local physical presence. The AML/CFT Risk Assessment 2020 classifies e-commerce manufacturing as low risk, so frontline risk-based supervision focuses on licensed international company service providers. However, an immediate on-site verification may be triggered by a suspicious transaction report or an adverse media alert.

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) - Registrar of International Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC1 (Application for Incorporation as an International Company) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; no escrow account required. The Company may declare any issued capital, with a minimum of one share and no maximum, and shares may be fully paid as agreed by the subscribers.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS: 1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION: The Company shall allot the shares set forth in the subscriber statement to the initial subscribers and issue certificates to them upon full payment. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company shall be located at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and the Registrar shall be notified of that address without delay. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The individuals named in the consent forms are appointed as the first directors, and a qualified secretary and any other officers are appointed, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting or until removed by the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online or written name reservation request to SIFA listing the desired company name ending in 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'. The Registry checks for conflicts with existing names and prohibited words. A reservation is valid for a specified period, and the name must be cleared before incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or prohibited character, file a revised name reservation or submit a written response to the Registrar's notice within 14 business days for reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent prepares the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, ensuring compliance with the International Companies Act 2008. Each subscriber executes the documents in the presence of a witness or notary. The registered agent confirms that the company is intended to be incorporated as an International Company.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association (signed by each subscriber)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the documents contain errors or incompatibilities, the registered agent will correct and re-submit them to the subscribers for re-execution before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of International Companies, SIFA, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed Memorandum and Articles, Form IC1, the registered agent's consent, and the prescribed government fee electronically through SIFA's online portal or in person at the registry counter. Payment may be made by bank transfer or direct deposit to the SIFA account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the application or requests further information, respond within 14 business days with clarifications, amended documents, or additional evidence; otherwise, the application may lapse.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and assigns a unique registration number. The Company is legally incorporated as an International Company on the date stated in the certificate. The registered agent obtains the original certificate and files it in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Approved incorporation file from the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed or contains clerical errors, submit a written request to SIFA for expedited issuance or correction under the rectification provisions of the International Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors / Licensed Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a board meeting, physically or by video conference, to adopt the first board resolutions covering share allotment, registered office adoption, appointment of directors, secretary, and officials, and authorization of bank account opening. Execute written minutes and consents.
required_dossiers: Consent forms for appointed directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum cannot be achieved, adopt a unanimous written resolution as permitted by the Articles of Association; if any appointment is declined, the board may appoint another qualified person by subsequent resolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – International Companies are restricted from carrying on business in Samoa under s.51 of the International Companies Act 2008 and therefore cannot obtain a local manufacturing license; any physical production must be conducted by a licensed third-party manufacturer in the country of production.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – no industrial operating or manufacturing permit is issued to an International Company for activities within Samoa.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Samoa Environment Division, Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable – the International Company has no physical facility or emissions in Samoa; any contracted manufacturer must satisfy its local EIA and pollution control requirements in its own jurisdiction.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable to the International Company itself. Contract manufacturers must comply with applicable wastewater, VOC, and hazardous waste standards enforced in their operating jurisdiction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for the International Company due to the absence of physical premises in Samoa. If the company later establishes a licensed representative office, it will require fire safety certification, structural load clearance, and workplace safety registration under Samoa law.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa — the central tax administration responsible for income tax, Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST), and stamp duty; official taxpayer portal: https://www.mfr.gov.ws (MfR Taxpayer Online Services).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987, the statutory TIN sequence is: (1) engage a SIFA-licensed registered agent to file the International Company incorporation application with the Registrar of International Companies; (2) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and register the registered office and registered agent particulars; (3) submit TIN registration Form TIN-01 to the Ministry for Revenue together with the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Association, registered agent consent, certified passport copies of directors and ultimate shareholders, and legal opinion as to non-resident offshore status; (4) receive the TIN certificate identifying the entity as a tax-exempt International Company; (5) apply for VAGST registration (Form VAGST-01) only if the IC makes taxable supplies in Samoa, which is ordinarily not applicable to offshore cosplay manufacturing sales; the foreign parent requires no separate Samoa TIN because the Samoan IC is the distinct legal taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — a Samoa International Company is statutorily exempt under section 154 of the International Companies Act 1987: it is deemed to carry on business exclusively outside Samoa, is non-resident for income tax purposes, and is exempt from Samoa income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, customs duty, and VAGST on offshore transactions; the entity is treated as corporate-level taxable only in its owner's jurisdiction, not in Samoa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) Domestic Company Election — an IC may elect by special resolution to redomicile under the Companies Act 2006 and become a Samoan resident ordinary company, thereby abandoning the IC tax exemption and becoming subject to the 25% corporate income tax and VAGST on domestic supplies. (2) No United States-style check-the-box election exists; Samoa does not provide single-entity pass-through classification for ICs. (3) Hybrid instrument election — the IC's governing documents may elect the legal character of shareholder advances/instruments to optimize source-country tax classification, and Samoa claims no unilateral hybrid-mismatch carveout; any conflict is resolved by the foreign jurisdiction's rules. (4) Registration for VAGST is elective for turnover below WST 70,000, allowing an IC voluntarily to register to recover input tax where local procurement occurs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 70,000 (Samoan Tala and Sene) of annual taxable turnover in Samoa; mandatory registration applies where taxable supplies and imports exceed this threshold, while foreign suppliers without a Samoa establishment are instead subject to reverse-charge obligations unless the supply qualifies for zero-rating as an offshore/export supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time national e-invoicing, fiscal digital stamping, or API-based continuous transaction control (CTC) clearance system is currently mandated in Samoa. Registered persons must issue sequential-numbered VAGST tax invoices, credit notes, and adjustment notes compliant with sections 15–17 of the VAGST Act 2008; returns and payments are filed electronically through the MfR online portal, and customs export data is captured in ASYCUDA World, but there is no government pre-approval or API clearance gate for individual invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods — including cosplay costumes, licensed theatrical robes, and synthetic wigs — are zero-rated under section 11 of the VAGST Act 2008 when the supplier retains proof that the goods were physically removed from Samoa and delivered to the foreign buyer within the customs-prescribed export period. Offshore services rendered to a non-resident outside Samoa likewise attract 0% VAGST. A Samoa International Company engaged in export-only cosplay manufacturing is outside the VAGST net: its export sales bear 0%, and any VAGST suffered on local ancillary inputs (freight, packing materials, negligible domestic services) may be recovered as input credit only if the supplier is VAGST-registered; otherwise it is a non-creditable cost. Goods exported duty-free may also qualify for a customs duty drawback on imported inputs used in manufacture under the Customs Act 2014.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World export entry) bearing the export entry number and date
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal of the goods from Samoa
Commercial Invoice matching the customs valuation
Packing List and Certificate of Origin (where required by the destination jurisdiction)
Foreign buyer purchase order and SWIFT payment confirmation
Inward Remittance Certificate or licensed bank credit advice evidencing final conversion and crediting of export proceeds to the IC's bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The MfR and Samoa Customs jointly audit export zero-rating claims under the VAGST Act 2008 and Customs Act 2014. Where export documentation is deficient, goods are diverted, or proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days, the export is recharacterized as a domestic supply: VAGST becomes payable at 15% retroactively to the original invoice date with interest at 2% per month or part-month. Fraudulent misuse of zero-rating or a false export declaration is a criminal tax evasion offence punishable by a fine of up to WST 50,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 7 years under section 65 of the VAGST Act 2008; Customs penalties may be up to three times the evaded amount with forfeiture of goods. For an International Company, such abuse triggers revocation of IC status under the International Companies Act 1987 by the Registrar of International Companies, causing retrospective loss of the tax-exempt zone classification and a look-back assessment of up to 6 years for income tax, VAGST, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), also operating as the Exchange Control Authority under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and Financial Institutions Act 1996.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tala (WST) operates under a managed float administered by the Central Bank of Samoa. Current account transactions (trade, services, interest, dividends below statutory thresholds) are generally convertible upon submission of supporting trade documentation. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment equity injections, intercompany debt, and remittance of liquidation proceeds, require prior exchange control permits from CBS. Samoa International Companies (ICs) that are non-resident owned and maintain no domestic business activity enjoy a statutory tax exemption; however, CBS still applies exchange control monitoring to any WST-denominated accounts. Profit remittance is permissible in the original currency of receipt without a mandatory conversion to WST, provided the payment is identified as a dividend from an IC and is made from a licensed external or foreign currency account. Full convertibility of the tala on the capital account is not available; case-by-case approval is required for capital outflows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBS Exchange Control regulations, all export receipts derived by a Samoa-resident entity must be repatriated to Samoa within 90 days of the later of shipment date or payment receipt. The full 100% of export proceeds must be sold to a licensed commercial bank for WST unless the exporter holds an approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) or External Account, in which case the surrender requirement is waived for the fund balance retained offshore. For International Companies that are non-resident and transact exclusively through an external account, the surrender rule does not apply; however, if any WST account is maintained, all foreign-currency inflows converted into WST must be declared to CBS on a monthly basis. Any conversion above USD 100,000 equivalent per single transaction requires prior CBS approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa does not currently issue electronic money institution (EMI) licenses or standalone fintech payment licenses. Payment services are restricted to banks and credit institutions licensed under the Financial Institutions Act 1996. Non-resident digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, or Airwallex may not establish a direct local settlement account in WST. They can be used by the Samoa IC only as offshore collection channels for retail card payments, subject to downstream settlement into a Samoa-licensed commercial bank account. No legal entity of the EMI may be registered as an authorized dealer or payment intermediary in Samoa.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person KYC interview is mandatory for all corporate account openings at Samoa-licensed banks. At least one director of the International Company, or an authorized signatory holding a valid power of attorney, must appear physically before the bank's compliance officer. The Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Notice (as revised) does not allow fully remote onboarding for non-resident companies. A registered agent in Samoa may act as an introduction channel, but the ultimate signatory directors must still undergo either an in-person interview at a Samoa branch or a video interview only if the bank has an existing relationship with a corresponding bank in the director's jurisdiction; in practice most Samoan banks require physical attendance for ICs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership of the International Company held by multiple non-resident discretionary trusts or family offices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of the IC's trust deed or registered agent statement, a legal opinion from a recognized law firm identifying the 25%+ ultimate beneficial owners, proof of source of wealth via audited financial statements or investment portfolio statements, and a signed AML undertaking that future transfers will be accompanied by tax and source-of-funds declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Declared business scope of cosplay costume production appears inconsistent with expected payment flows from Stripe and Shopify
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business narrative with product SKU lists, supplier contracts for synthetic fabrics and wigs, an e-commerce sales dashboard export from Shopify, purchase orders or licensing agreements for theatrical or cosplay IP, and logistics contracts with international freight forwarders; all documents to be notarized and apostilled.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume small-value cross-border e-commerce receipts triggering uncharacteristic credit patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly reconciliation between Shopify Payments and Stripe settlement reports and the bank account; a standard chargeback and refund policy; an external audit opinion confirming the entity is a pass-through manufacturing supplier; and a customer jurisdiction breakdown by payment currency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions routed through third-party payment aggregators without direct bank-to-bank wire references
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid contracts with Stripe, Inc. and Shopify Inc. obtained in the respective merchant of record agreements; gateway transaction logs; an explanation of the settlement currency (USD or EUR) and conversion methodology; and a letter from the Samoa registered agent confirming that the IC is in good standing and entitled to receive foreign trade income.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or adverse media screening flags on end customers located in jurisdictions not recognized by Samoa exchange control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A consolidated know-your-customer (KYC) report from the payment gateways for the relevant customer base; an end-user license declaration confirming cosplay costumes are non-military and non-dual-use; and an independent screening report from a commercial database (e.g., Dow Jones, World-Check) covering the company, its directors, and the top 10 destination countries.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Samoa International Company, all inbound capital injections must be received through a licensed commercial bank account in Samoa via SWIFT MT103/MT202. The wire instruction must use the beneficiary account name exactly matching the IC's Certificate of Incorporation. The payment purpose field must reference 'ISIC 3240 – Capital Contribution to International Company' and include the Samoa International Company registration number (e.g., IC-XXXX). For amounts exceeding USD 100,000 equivalent, the Samoa receiving bank will require a copy of the exchange control approval letter from CBS or a declaration that the funds represent a non-resident shareholder loan/equity qualifying for automatic approval under the Exchange Control (General) Exemption Notice. All inbound wire confirmations must be supported by a source-of-funds statement (bank reference from the remitting bank) and an undertaking that the capital is used solely for the company's legitimate foreign trade activities.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail for outbound trade settlements is the SWIFT network via Samoa-licensed correspondent banks. Payments to overseas suppliers are executed as SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers with full reconciliation. For letters of credit (LCs), the Samoa bank will advise or confirm commercial LCs on behalf of the International Company under UCP 600. The company will typically open an LC from its external account funded by USD/EUR balances, with the counterparty presenting documents through their confirming bank. For low-value e-commerce refunds and chargebacks on cosplay apparel, the IC may use the Stripe and Shopify Payments settlement rails directly, but aggregated refund payouts must not create a WST deficit in the Samoa operational account. The bank will require monthly reconciliation of all outbound disbursements against purchase orders, bills of lading, and warehouse receipts. High-value trade disbursements above USD 50,000 equivalent must include a copy of the commercial invoice, packing list, and shipping proof to avoid exchange control penalties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward currency contracts with a Samoa-licensed commercial bank, permitted for current account trade transactions with a maximum maturity of 12 months and genuine underlying export/import exposure.
Cross-currency swaps between WST and USD/EUR approved on a case-by-case basis by the Central Bank of Samoa for capital account items or long-term supply contracts.
FX swaps with a licensed bank for short-term liquidity management (up to 6 months), subject to daily CBS position reporting.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible onshore; however, offshore non-resident counterparties may transact in WST-based NDFs outside Samoa without CBS regulatory approval, provided the Samoa IC does not directly book the NDF in its Samoa bank account.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form IC-AR) under the International Companies Act 2012
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of WST 50 per month (or equivalent) and continued default for 6 months may result in a Registrar's compliance notice and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Duty (Annual Government Licence Renewal) for International Company status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MCIL International Companies Registry, made through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each anniversary of incorporation; no grace period unless a fee-payment extension is granted by the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 10% late-payment surcharge is imposed on the overdue duty; if the annual duty remains unpaid for 90 days, the Registrar may commence strike-off proceedings without prior notice, causing dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (AML/CFT UBO Register Update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MCIL International Companies Registry and Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (upon request), through the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the anniversary date; any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be notified to the registered agent within 14 calendar days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Act 2019, carrying court-imposed fines and, for natural persons, imprisonment; persistent default is also a discretionary strike-off trigger.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to a Samoa International Company merely by revenue, asset or shareholder thresholds; a statutory audit may be triggered only by the company's articles, a shareholders' resolution, a Registrar direction, or a separate regulatory licence condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS and IFRS for SMEs as adopted by the Samoa Institute of Accountants; the International Companies Act 2012 requires books to give a true and fair view where financial statements are prepared.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must maintain and annually confirm the beneficial ownership register by the incorporation anniversary. All share transfers must be recorded in the register and reported to the agent within 14 days, and any resulting UBO changes must be reflected in the annual confirmation. The register is confidential but must be produced to MCIL or the Financial Intelligence Unit on lawful demand.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$250–US$850 per annum (registered agent and office fee for a standard International Company)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$1,500–US$5,000 per annum if a voluntary audit is required by shareholders, lenders, or Stripe/Shopify Payments onboarding; otherwise US$0 (not statutorily mandated)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies (ICs) registered under the International Companies Act 1987 are exempt from Samoan income tax on all income derived from outside Samoa. No corporate income tax is imposed on offshore-sourced profits, and no capital gains tax applies. A permanent zero-rate regime applies to qualifying non-resident-owned ICs conducting no local business.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return is required for a tax-exempt International Company. Annual compliance is satisfied through the IC Annual Return / Declaration of Compliance filed with the Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) Registry Portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Return must be filed within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation. No tax return deadline applies because no taxable income is recognized for offshore-sourced income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1: Company Name and Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name and unique SIFSA registration number of the International Company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter exactly as stated on the certificate of incorporation. Non-resident owners are not separately registered for Samoan tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Licensed Samoan registered agent's name, license number, and contact address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent must be physically present in Samoa and authorized to act for the non-resident-owned IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical registered office address in Samoa, typically the registered agent's premises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PO Box alone is insufficient. The address must be a physical location where legal documents can be served.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, nationalities, and residential addresses of all directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide certified passport copies and proof of residential address for each non-resident beneficial owner. Nominee directors may be disclosed to the agent only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5: Declaration of No Local Business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory declaration confirming the company has not carried on business in Samoa and derives no Samoan-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This declaration is critical. If the cosplay apparel business involves Samoan customers, local sales, or Samoan-based activities, the IC risks losing its exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized and issued share capital, share classes, and consideration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum paid-up capital is required. Non-resident ownership may be 100%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of payment of the prescribed SIFSA annual fee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent must confirm payment. Non-payment can lead to late fees and strike-off.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the registered agent has obtained and updated all know-your-customer and beneficial ownership documents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must provide source-of-funds documentation for any capital injections or digital payment flows.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is SAT 100 for the first month and SAT 50 for each subsequent month, capped at SAT 250. Non-payment of annual fee may result in reinstatement fees, late penalties, and strike-off with assets vesting in the Government of Samoa.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Statutory dividend WHT is nil because the IC's income is wholly offshore-sourced. To claim DTA relief on any residual Samoan-source exposure, a non-resident shareholder must submit a Samoan tax form TR-1 together with the treaty partner's Certificate of Residence, a declaration of beneficial ownership, and the company's solvency certificate. The Ministry of Revenue will confirm treaty rate applicability; most Samoa DTAs reduce dividend WHT to 5% or 15% depending on shareholding and treaty terms.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory interest WHT is 15% on Samoan-source interest paid to non-residents; royalties paid for use of IP in Samoa are subject to 15% WHT (or 10% under certain DTAs). Where royalty or interest income is derived from outside Samoa and paid by the IC, 0% Samoan WHT applies. Treaty relief must be claimed through TR-1 and supporting TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory SAT-denominated threshold is codified. Samoa has no mandatory Local File / Master File filing regime for International Companies. However, if the IC transacts with a Samoan resident or related party, transfer pricing documentation must be prepared based on OECD principles to substantiate arm's length pricing and protect 0% exemption status. Such records must be retained at the registered office for 5 years.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa has not enacted a standalone Economic Substance Regulation regime, but SIFSA and the Tax Administration impose a substance-over-form doctrine. An IC must demonstrate a physical registered office, a licensed agent, board decisions documented outside Samoa, and genuine commercial activity conducted outside Samoa. A cosplay prop and apparel manufacturing IC must show real foreign distribution contracts, procurement, and invoicing substance; otherwise it may be treated as a sham, subject to strike-off, or taxed as a Samoan resident.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Misrepresentation of Offshore Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deriving Samoan-source income from local cosplay apparel sales but filing the IC Annual Return declaring zero business activity in Samoa and failing to register for Samoan income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 2016, evading tax attracts a penalty of 150% of the tax evaded, plus interest at 2% per month; criminal conviction carries a fine up to SAT 400,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs a false declaration may be personally liable for the company's unpaid tax, subject to asset freeze orders, travel bans, and imprisonment for up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Samoan IC with no economic substance as a mere invoicing conduit for online cosplay costume sales to reduce global taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SIFSA may revoke the IC status, impose fines of SAT 10,000 per non-compliance, and strike the company off; foreign tax authorities may recharacterize the structure and impose withholding or anti-avoidance taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for company debts and tax liabilities; if fraud is proven, they face Director disqualification orders and travel bans under mutual assistance litigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving Stripe or Shopify Payments from online cosplay sales without adequate source-of-funds verification, or moving funds through Samoan banks without disclosing beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's AML/CFT Act 2018, fines up to SAT 1,000,000 per offence; banks may close accounts, and suspicious transactions are reported to the FIU; criminal money laundering charges carry penalties of up to SAT 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 14 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal asset confiscation, seizure of digital payment proceeds, travel bans, and imprisonment for 10–14 years may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Misuse of Tax Loss Carry-Forward or Improper Records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming tax loss carry-forwards on a Samoan corporate tax return while the IC is exempt, or failing to maintain accurate accounting records for the cosplay manufacturing business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of SAT 50,000 for failure to keep records, plus daily default penalty of SAT 500; the exemption may be backdated and revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable to pay penalties and may be sentenced to imprisonment for up to 3 years for failure to maintain proper books.
